issues.body: The Claude branch still computes `content = (event.get("message") or {}).get("content")` and only examines blocks when `content` is a list. A missing/falsey message, missing content, or non-list content leaves `unclassified` false, so a following known `result` satisfies the measurement gates and emits an empty count map as `probe:0`. A truthy non-dict message instead raises at `.get`, preventing best-effort telemetry output. For known tool-bearing blocks, `name = str(block.get("name", ""))` converts a missing or non-string protocol field into `other`, preserving a confident zero probe even though the malformed record cannot be safely classified. The new tests exercise an unknown block type, but not these malformed shapes.
issues.fix_hint: Require every Claude `assistant` event to contain an object `message` whose `content` is a list; otherwise set `unclassified = True` without raising. For every block in `CLAUDE_BLOCK_TOOLS`, require `name` to be a string before classification; missing/non-string names must invalidate the measurement. Add negative fixtures followed by `result` for missing/non-list assistant content, a truthy non-object message, and a tool block with missing/non-string name; each must omit `probe`, while the complete tool-free Claude fixture must continue to emit `probe:0`.
issues.title: Malformed Claude assistant payloads can still fabricate probe zero

verdict.summary: The round-3 fail-closed finding remains unresolved. Claude `assistant` events still validate neither the `message`/`content` container shape nor the tool-name type. Consequently malformed assistant payloads can still be treated as fully classified and, when followed by `result`, publish a confident `probe:0`; a truthy non-object `message` can additionally crash the parser at `.get`. The added negative fixtures cover renamed block discriminators but not the malformed container/name cases identified previously. This is materially the same major issue at the same severity, so progress is stagnant.
